public_rationale: CBRE reported that 80.4% of under-construction capacity was preleased in H1 2026, before the July 22 forecast [e1]. These commitments do not establish sustained paid use after the relevant pipeline opens [e1]. Moody’s July 31, 2026 analysis explains why construction completion need not produce cash flow, but does not establish a market-wide demand shortage [e2]. Neither source establishes representative post-commissioning payments and operating results for the relevant pipeline, so the forecast remains unresolved [e1, e2].
limitations: CBRE measures a broader data-center market, not a defined cohort of AI projects underway at publication.
The evidence does not establish substantial commissioning or sustained occupancy, paid usage, collections and financial viability for that cohort.
The forecast specifies no deadline, project cohort or economic viability threshold.
Power and construction delays do not establish insufficient paying demand.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: When data centers under construction come online, the market will not support the number of paying customers they need.

statement.excerpt: Eventually, these data centers (which are taking 18-36 months to complete) will start turning on, which will require them to start having paying customers at a scale that the market can’t actually support.

from_speaker: paying customers at a scale that the market can’t actually support
our_interpretation: These data centers means the AI-oriented construction pipeline funded or underway when the post appeared.
The ordinary reading is a market-wide shortage of sustainable paying demand as that pipeline opens, rather than a claim that every facility will fail.
Commissioning is the forecast's observation setting, not a separate optional antecedent.
The construction duration is not a deadline measured from publication.
Paying demand requires actual payments and sustained use; preleases alone do not establish it.
criteria.support_condition: Representative operating evidence from the publication-date pipeline shows persistent demand-driven vacancies, insufficient paid use or customer payment shortfalls that prevent the new capacity from being sustained.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evidence after substantial commissioning shows sustained paying demand sufficient to support the new capacity and its operating and financing obligations.

evidence.locator: State of the Market, preleasing paragraph
evidence.explanation: Strong preleasing is material evidence against assuming that the pipeline lacks prospective tenants. It measures broader first-half commitments, not sustained payments after the forecasted facilities open.
This analysis identifies a genuine distinction between construction completion and commercial operation. It does not demonstrate a market-wide shortage of paying customers.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Representative results after substantial commissioning of the publication-date pipeline, showing whether sustained paid usage and collections cover operating and financing obligations. The evidence must distinguish demand shortfalls from power, permitting and construction delays.
